summary: Resubmitted the startup committed-log replay experiment after the source-range rejection: the four offending IDs now either reuse their registered excerpts exactly (api_restore_call 600-610, api_start_goroutines 630-640, raft_batch_flush 1336-1362) or were replaced by a new ID (store_commit_interface, log.go 194-221 for the CommitTrackingLogStore interface), and every reused ID was checked field-for-field against the registered material. The harness exp_restore_midband_test.go is unchanged and locally verified: a real single-node prefix that commits 200 commands, snapshots at index 202 and then commits a second batch, restarted against the retained stores, returns in 1 ms with a 50-batch tail (3198 entries), returns in 3 ms at exactly the 128-batch channel capacity (8192 entries), and does not return within 20 s at 129 batches (8194 entries) with one goroutine parked in processLogs. That measures the previously missing middle of the replay range on cluster-produced state and brackets the capacity boundary with the tail differing by a single entry, so the stall cannot be attributed to replay volume or slowness. The request declares three case events as prerequisites with replay_batches conditions and asserts returned == true on each result event; it validates against submission.schema.json.
